Unfortunately, during this time my experience has often been more negative than positive. I have seen many different doctors and receptionists over the years, but the same issues with professionalism seem to continue.

In particular, some of the reception staff can come across as unprofessional and at times quite rude towards patients. It sometimes feels as though they forget that patients come to the practice because they need help and support. Instead of feeling assisted, patients can feel dismissed or undermined.

As a kidney patient, I need repeat medication and must provide letters from the hospital to support my requests. Despite doing this, I have found it difficult to receive the help I need, and I often feel that my concerns are not properly listened to. I have made several complaints in the past, yet I have never received a response or any follow-up to address the issues.

Living with chronic kidney disease is already stressful, and I have also undergone tests for cancer. The last thing I need is additional stress when trying to access essential medical care.

I truly hope the practice improves its professionalism, communication, and the way patients are treated. My experience with this practice has been deeply concerning due to repeated administrative failures affecting essential diabetes care. Most recently, my repeat prescription for Humulin insulin — requested through the NHS App two days in advance — was not approved. When I called the surgery, I was told it had been referred for review and was advised to call back the next day. I had to explain that I was completely out of insulin and that my next injection was due that evening before the prescription was finally issued.

For a Type 1 diabetic, insulin is life-sustaining medication. Delays or barriers to accessing it are not minor administrative issues — they carry immediate clinical risk. Being told to “call back tomorrow” when a patient has no insulin left demonstrates a worrying lack of urgency around continuity of care for chronic conditions.

Unfortunately, this is not an isolated incident. Since registering with this practice I have experienced multiple problems affecting essential diabetes supplies, including a CGM prescription request not being processed (leaving me without monitoring for several days), initial refusal of basic glucose testing equipment, and repeated challenges around routine diabetes medication.

Patients who depend on timely access to essential medication should be aware that delays and barriers can occur here.
